To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a fluorescent derivative of atractyloside, 6'-O- fluorescein-ATP, is a high affinity, specific ligand of the mitochondrial AD/ATP translocae (AAT).

the binding of a fluorescent probe to AAT stabilizes the dimeric conformation of the protein, and that use of the fluorescent derivative in the purification protocol enables the dimeric form of AAT to be purified more effectively.
a fluorescent derivative of ATR, FATR, has been used to purify AAT to homogeneity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methodology that enables the purification of a stable form of a protein, in this case AAT.
the development of an efficient purification method for AAT that can be used to study the structure of AAT and its interactions with ligands.
the development of a purification procedure for AAT that uses a specific inhibitor of AAT, ATR, to stabilize and purify the AAT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the binding of the fluorescent derivative of ATR, FATR, to AAT has allowed the purification of a stable dimeric form of AAT that is devoid of other members in the mitochondrial carrier family and that is in a single major stable conformation.
the presence of FATR on the AAT stabilizes the protein and allows the purification of highly pure AAT.

the use of a fluorescent ATR derivative has allowed the purification of highly pure AAT, and that the purification protocol has been optimized to allow the purification of the stable dimer of the inhibited protein, and the purification of the monomer of uninhibited AAT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of fluorescent ATR derivatives has allowed the development of a purification protocol that yields pure, monomeric, conformationally stable AAT.

the binding of ATR derivatives to AAT results in a stable dimeric conformation of the protein that is more easily solubilized and purified than the unbound monomer, and this is a general phenomenon that may be exploited in the purification of other members of this family.
the presence of a bound fluorescent probe enabled us to stabilize the dimeric AIT and to develop a simple, rapid and effective purification protocol.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of a fluorescent probe on a high-affinity ligand for a protein allows the liganded protein to be purified to high purity, and in the case of AAT, in a conformation that is different from the unligand protein, and which is stable to chromatographic conditions.
the use of a fluorescent ATR derivative can be used to stabilize AAT during chromatographic steps, allowing the purification of highly pure AAT.
the binding of a fluorescent probe can be exploited to stabilize and purify mitochondrial carriers.
